source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Precautions applied only after a laboratory confirms a transmissible infection, with no measures used for other patients.","B":"Hand hygiene, exposure-based PPE, respiratory hygiene, injection safety, and safe handling of contaminated equipment and surfaces.","C":"Hand hygiene alone, because PPE, respiratory hygiene, sharps safety and injection practices are separate from Standard Precautions.","D":"Airborne isolation for every patient, including respirators and negative-pressure rooms regardless of diagnosis or anticipated exposure."}}
source_row.rationale: Standard Precautions apply to all patient care and include hand hygiene, risk-based PPE, respiratory hygiene, injection/sharps safety, equipment reprocessing and environmental cleaning.
source_row.source_detail: Standard Precautions page lists hand hygiene, PPE based on exposure risk, respiratory hygiene/cough etiquette, sharps safety, safe injection practices, sterile instruments/devices and environmental cleaning. Current CDC infection-control guidance rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.source_name: CDC — Standard Precautions for All Patient Care
source_row.stem: Which set of practices is included in CDC Standard Precautions for routine patient care?
